## TL;DR

A running close-out attempt now writes its own progress log and keeps its step, host and
last-progress time on the job record. `GET /api/tasks/<id>/integration-job` returns them,
the pipeline snapshot carries them to the card, status bar and drawer, and a retry shows
the reason the attempt it replaced failed, in the copy tooltip. A stopped writer is flagged
as possibly stuck. Review round 1 closed three gaps: the retry reason was API-only, late
heartbeats could stamp a finished record, and step changes waited for the next stage event.

## Work and rationale

The integration log was only written when a gate check failed, so a job validating for 55
minutes looked the same as a hung one. I added `src/server/close-out-progress.ts`, a
`CloseOutProgressRecorder` that the orchestrator creates for each `processJob` run. It:

- Appends to `.repoos/logs/integration/<id>-attempt-<n>.log`: a start line, one line per
  step change, a heartbeat at least every 15 seconds, and an end line that names the outcome.
- Polls the live remote run every 5 seconds for its host and stage. The remote-run registry
  already records both, so no new callbacks went through the remote pool.
- Persists `step`, `host`, `lastProgressAt` and `progressLogPath` to the job record, scoped
  to the attempt by the existing `expectedAttempt` guard.

The orchestrator reports local steps through one `reportStep` helper, a no-op without a
recorder. `processJob` is now a wrapper around the unchanged body, `runJobPhases`.

Design choices a reviewer should check:

- **Heartbeat, not stage events, drives "alive".** The 5-second stage heartbeat only runs
  inside long stages, so it cannot prove liveness across sync or the queue wait.
- **Stale means the writer stopped.** `progressStale` is set when the last write is 90 seconds
  old on an active attempt. A quiet remote test run still heartbeats and is not flagged.
- **Retries.** `enqueue` already makes a new attempt generation on a failed re-enqueue. I
  added `previousFailure` (attempt, reason, failedAt) to that record, set only when the
  replaced record was `failed`. A cancel does not set it.

Review round 1 fixes:

- **Retry reason in the UI.** `integrationRetryNote` builds "Attempt 2 — attempt 1 failed:
  <first line of reason>", and `integrationActiveCopy` appends it to the title. The card,
  status bar and drawer all call that helper, so the reason reaches all three.
- **Terminal records are final.** `progressWritable(phase)` is false for `done`, `failed`
  and a missing record. The recorder's persist path checks it, so a heartbeat that fires
  after `failed` cannot stamp a live step or a fresh timestamp.
- **Push on change.** The recorder calls `onChange` after each persisted step or host
  change. The orchestrator's new last constructor argument, `onAttemptProgress`, is wired in
  `server.ts` to `emitIntegration()`. A throwing observer cannot disturb the recorder.

The copy helper keeps existing labels unchanged when a job has no step, host or attempt.

## Approaches tried

I first considered reusing `<id>-<checkAttempt>.log`. That name holds the full transcript
of a failed gate run (#0428), so the attempt-scoped name `<id>-attempt-<n>.log` keeps the two
separate.

## Challenges and blockers

- Earlier gate runs failed on unrelated tests. `checks-live-run-responsive` (WebKit, 375 px)
  waited a fixed 150 ms before measuring. On a loaded shared runner that raced the render. It
  passed alone locally. I replaced both sleeps with `settledLayout`, which measures until two
  consecutive reports agree and still asserts the last report if the layout never settles.
  The final scoped gate passed on `mini` with 247 of 247 files and the browser gate.
- One runner infra failure (`thinkpad`, exit 255) fell back to `mini` and passed.
- The first local typecheck showed many errors in untouched files. The gate's own run was
  clean, so I read those as a different TypeScript resolution in my shell.

## Key learnings

- `readJob` copies job fields one by one, so a new job field not added there is silently
  dropped on read. The round-trip test pins each new field.
- The attempt generation is the right key for a log file and for "is this a retry?". The
  per-check counter goes up per gate run, so it is not an attempt identity.
- The server's stale flag and the UI idle timer overlap. Both stay: the flag is precise and the
  idle timer covers legacy jobs that have no recorder.

## Not done in this change

- `done/total` test progress: the remote runner does not stream a total.
- The #1272 card timer: `startedAt` is exposed, but the timer is unchanged.
- Browser screenshots: no preview was requested, so the UI is covered by copy-helper tests.
- `previousFailure` persists on a `done` record. It is harmless, since the snapshot only
  surfaces active jobs.
